title: Hate Speech Detection with Generalizable Target-aware Fairness
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the fairness of hate speech detection (HSD) models, specifically the performance discrepancy (in terms of false positive and false negative rates) across posts targeting different identity groups, including religious groups. The goal was to ensure the HSD classifier does not become biased against content merely mentioning a specific religion.
base_benchmarks: Jigsaw Unintended Bias in Toxicity Classification
findings: The proposed method, GetFair, demonstrated superior fairness and generalizability in hate speech detection for posts targeting religious groups (Christian, Jewish, Muslim) compared to several state-of-the-art baselines. It was particularly effective at maintaining fairness for 'unseen' religious targets (e.g., 'Muslim' in one test setting) that were not present in the training data, indicating a strong ability to avoid spurious correlations between religious terms and hateful content.
